title: Sessionization heuristics and denormalized invocation slices for latency anomaly analysis
creator: Diego Morales
description:
Problem: Current console analytics surface struggles to attribute tail latency spikes to tenant-level invocation patterns because events are highly denormalized across callstream, route metadata, and kernel scheduler logs. Goal: design and build a deterministic sessionization layer and a set of denormalized invocation slices (per-session and per-route denorm tables) that make latency anomaly investigation fast and dependable for SREs and PMs.

Scope:
- Define canonical session boundaries across websocket/HTTP requests, background retries, and batched invocations using conservative heuristics (idle gap + route-change + batch-id grouping).
- Produce a tenant-scoped denorm_invocation_slice table optimized for fast OLAP and ad-hoc debugging: one row per logical invocation (session_id + invocation_index) with normalized dimensions (tenant, route_id, model_variant, config_hash) and aggregated metrics (p50/p95/p99 latency, token_count, kernel_time, queue_time, KV-cache_hit_rate).
- Implement late-arrival/ordering repair using event watermarking and idempotent upserts to a snapshot layer (delta + compact) to avoid double-counting in weekly aggregates.
- Add tenant-level cost attribution fields (estimated_gpu_ms, token_units) to enable per-route cost dashboards.

Data sources: callstream events (proto), kernel-scheduler logs, kvcache telemetry, route metadata service, billing-metering stream.

Non-goals: full session reconstruction across offline ingestion windows >72h, realtime per-tenant SLA enforcement (separate infra).
acceptance_criteria: A canonical session_id algorithm documented and agreed in Confluence (deterministic across replay)
Denorm table (denorm_invocation_slice) produced daily with schema matching PRD and sample rows for 100 tenants
Late-arrival window (72h) handled without double-counting in weekly cost rollups
End-to-end perf: query p95 on denorm_invocation_slice for a single tenant (30d) < 3s using existing BigQuery materialized views
Integration tests for idempotent upsert and ordering repair added to pipeline CI
updates: 2025-02-11: Kickoff with Console analytics, Runtime, and Billing teams. Agreed on 72h late-arrival window and tenant-scoped denorm table as primary deliverable.
2025-02-13: Prototype session_id algorithm: hash(tenant_id, first_event_ts_bucketed, route_fingerprint) with idle_gap=45s. Benchmarked uniqueness on sample of 10M events; collision rate < 1e-7.

2025-02-17: Data model v1 drafted. Fields: session_id, invocation_index, start_ts, end_ts, tenant_id, route_id, model_variant, config_hash, tokens_in, tokens_out, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms, kernel_ms, queue_ms, kv_cache_hit_pct, estimated_gpu_ms, token_units, ingestion_watermark_ts, source_files. Schema posted in Confluence.

2025-02-20: Implemented streaming upsert job in warehouse repo (PR referenced). Upsert is idempotent via composite key (tenant_id, session_id, invocation_index). Using staged delta + compaction every 6h.

2025-02-24: Ran end-to-end job for first 100 tenants. Verified cost fields correlate with billing-metering within 3% on sample routes. Observed ~0.8% of events arriving >24h late; added repair path to re-run compaction on affected partitions.

2025-02-27: Performance tuning: added sparse partitioning by tenant tier and route_family. Query latency for 30d tenant slice improved from 6.5s to 2.6s. Preparing PR for materialized view definitions and documentation.
comments: PM review (Aisha Khan) 2025-02-14: Please ensure the sessionization rules are reversible for audit — we need the original event ids preserved in the denorm table.
Design feedback (Lena Wu) 2025-02-18: Suggest adding route_fingerprint dimension to make rollups stable when route metadata evolves.
SRE note (Ben Carter) 2025-02-25: For latency attribution, include kernel_queue_histogram buckets in the denorm as compressed JSON; helps quick drilldowns.

Architectural review (Ravi Singh) 2025-02-26: Ensure the upsert path uses monotonic watermarks to avoid race conditions with streaming consumers. Consider a lightweight CDC consumer to keep materialized views near-realtime.
